editorial:
In 1967 Los Angeles, a widowed mother named Alice runs a fake séance business with her two daughters, Lina and Doris. When they add a Ouija board to their act, Doris starts talking to spirits and things turn real fast. The movie follows this small family as they try to save Doris from a dark force that has taken over their home. It has an old-school horror feel, with creepy rooms, quiet tension, and a strong emotional core about a family in danger.

The acting is a big reason this works, especially Lulu Wilson as Doris and Annalise Basso as Lina. The pacing starts slow, then builds into scary moments that feel earned. The period details look great, and the scares are more about dread than cheap jumps. It can feel familiar if you have seen many possession movies, but it still delivers. Watch it if you like creepy family horror. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: Doris becomes fully possessed and turns violent against her family and Father Tom. The priest is killed, Alice is badly hurt, and Lina has to stab Doris to stop the demon. Doris dies, but the evil is not completely gone. Lina survives, yet she is left traumatized and institutionalized, with the final scenes hinting that the dark force may still be nearby.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy possession horror and old-school scares.
